name: MD-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by roughly 31 points, among the bluest House seats in the country
Incumbent Kweisi Mfume is running with about $656,000 on hand; Scott Collier shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price roughly a 96% Democratic win probability
Incumbent was renominated with no sign of a competitive primary
model.rationale: The district's 31-point Democratic lean, Mfume's incumbency and clear financial edge, and markets pricing a heavy Democratic favorite all point the same way, and no polls or expert ratings suggest any complication.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development, such as a major scandal or a sudden surge of outside spending behind the challenger, would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 7th District, anchored in Baltimore, is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 31 points toward Democrats. Kweisi Mfume, a longtime figure in Maryland politics, holds the seat and was renominated. He enters the general election with about $656,000 on hand, while Republican Scott Collier shows no reported fundraising or cash reserves.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put Democratic odds around 96 percent, consistent with the district's heavy Democratic lean. The expected margin is roughly 29 points for Mfume, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling. A Republican victory would require an unprecedented shift in this district.
